thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Automated alert: unusual KMS decrypt activity detected for project redwood-prod in us-west1. 30 distinct consumer identities performed decrypts in a 10m window. Alert score: HIGH

maria-ops: Seeing same in our console — looks like cross-region decrypts from a service account that shouldn't be used for customer keys.

raj-security: On it. Can someone confirm which keyring/key ids? I have a suspicion about the migration job that ran last night.

maria-ops: Key details: projects/redwood-prod/locations/us-west1/keyRings/customer-keys/cryptoKeys/cust-key-v2. Logged origin IPs include ec2-54-88-... and some GCP worker ranges.

olivia-eng: The nightly migration task touched the KMS wrapper service. I’m pausing that job now: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/migration-runner -n infra`

maria-ops: Paused. Also rotated the KMS key primary version to disable prior versions from being used for decrypts: `gcloud kms keys versions destroy 3 --key cust-key-v2 --keyring customer-keys --location us-west1 --project redwood-prod` (keeping a snapshot for forensics).

raj-security: Good. Immediate containment checklist:
- revoke tokens for migration-runner service account
- disable cross-region key permissions
- enable verbose audit logging on KMS and access to IAM logs

maria-ops: Revoked SA keys: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable <key-id> --iam-account=migration-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

olivia-eng: Confirmed we removed `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` binding from the migration-runner SA.

kevin-ciso: Notifying execs. Drafting a short advisory for leadership: "We detected anomalous decrypt activity involving one customer-managed KMS key. Immediate containment actions taken; no evidence yet of plaintext exfiltration. Incident response team investigating root cause and scope. Will update in 2 hours or sooner." Thoughts?

sarah-comms: For external messaging — we should avoid technicalities. Suggested customer-facing line: "We observed unusual access patterns to a customer-managed encryption key and have taken steps to secure keys and investigate. There is currently no confirmed impact to customer data; we will notify affected customers promptly if we confirm any exposure"

raj-security: Agree. But we must be ready if we find data exposure. Assigning tasks: forensics (maria + olivia), IAM/RBAC review (raj), audit log collection (maria), customer-impact analysis (sarah).

maria-ops: Collected logs: exported KMS audit logs and IAM logs to secure GCS bucket `gs://sec-incident-1758504321` with restricted ACLs. Running grep on access patterns now.

olivia-eng: I’m spinning up a read-only snapshot of the database backups to run a quick check for unusual decrypt calls from stored artifacts. Won't modify backups.

raj-security: Observations from initial triage: 25 of the consumer identities are internal worker accounts; 5 are unknown ephemeral tokens minted from an external CI provider used by a partner. That partner integration was updated last week.

kevin-ciso: Put legal and compliance on standby. If partner-originated tokens are implicated we need contract review.

sarah-comms: Draft of internal advisory for staff (short):
"Internal Advisory: We detected anomalous KMS decrypt activity tied to a customer-managed key. Containment is in place (rotation + SA revocation). Incident team is investigating scope and impact. Do not share details externally. We will provide an update at 18:30 PT."

maria-ops: For root cause we have two leads: 1) migration-runner had stale credentials cached in a sidecar 2) partner CI mistakenly had permission to impersonate a SA.

olivia-eng: Found evidence of a cached token in migration-runner logs around 02:12: `DEBUG token refresh failed, using cached token` — we rotated tokens but apparently the sidecar kept the cached creds. Pushing a hotfix to clear caches.

maria-ops: Hotfix applied: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/migration-runner -n infra` and removed the sidecar image that had the credential caching behavior.

raj-security: For post-incident actions (PIs):
- Audit all RBAC bindings in redwood-prod for `cloudkms.*` permissions
- Add automated policy to block non-service-network regions for decrypt ops
- Increase KMS audit log retention to 90d in sec-only bucket
- Add E2E test that verifies no SA caches credentials in migration tasks

kevin-ciso: Approve that list. Also propose a short exec update:
"We contained a KMS key misuse event within 30 minutes. Key rotation and IAM removals mitigated immediate risk. Investigation ongoing; no confirmed data exposure. Post-incident measures include RBAC hardening, log retention increases, and partner contract review."

sarah-comms: Customer notification template (for affected partner customers):
"We are writing to inform you of an event related to access activity for a customer-managed encryption key. We took immediate measures to secure the key and are conducting a thorough investigation. At this time there is no evidence of plaintext data exposure. We will provide a follow-up within 48 hours with findings and any recommended actions."

maria-ops: Quick status: forensics found no decrypted object downloads to external endpoints. All decrypt calls match internal VPC IP ranges except the 5 ephemeral partner tokens which were scoped to decrypt only.

raj-security: Starting vulnerability triage for the migration-runner sidecar pattern — tagging as P1 for our backlog. Need owner for remediation plan and timeline.

olivia-eng: I can own remediation and will propose a schedule by EOD. Plan: 1) remove caching sidecar permanently; 2) implement token rotation enforcement; 3) add integration tests.

kevin-ciso: Good. Capture all decisions in the incident tracker and prepare a full timeline for the postmortem. We’ll run an incident review with DRI stakeholders tomorrow.

sarah-comms: Will finalize exec advisory and customer template. Please flag any language edits by 17:30 PT.

maria-ops: Closing note — evidence so far indicates no customer data breach. Continuing to monitor and will escalate if new findings appear. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> HIGH, status -> contained, incident_id -> INC-2026-0452

raj-security: Thanks everyone. Filing follow-ups: `#action: RBAC audit (raj)`, `#action: Forensics report (maria)`, `#action: Remediation plan (olivia)`, `#action: Customer comms (sarah)`.

maria-ops: I'll upload forensic artifacts and KMS log exports to the secure case folder and link in the incident tracker.

olivia-eng: EOD update: remediation plan drafted, ETA for code changes 3 days, tests and deploys 7 days.

kevin-ciso: We'll brief board security liaison tomorrow morning. Thanks all for quick response."
